cases.remaining_requirement: Recover the versioned TOGOM3136 or original JCM242 record that supports this exact ATCC-labelled occurrence, including product identifier and addition volume; decide which stock the frozen import intended.
cases.reasoning: The frozen JCM242 occurrence calls the additive ATCC Trace Mineral Supplement, whereas current JCM242 specifies the trace minerals of JCM151. Official ATCC MD-TMS is an EDTA/cobalt-nitrate formulation; JCM151 uses nitrilotriacetate and cobalt sulfate. These are demonstrably different stocks. The frozen 10 g/L field does not identify a product or resolve this conflict.

cases.remaining_requirement: Recovered supernatant volume, soluble yield and organism/product detail remain unreported; proposed process identity does not claim those analytical properties.
cases.reasoning: NBRC1407 defines a preparation made by boiling 250 g dried baker yeast in 1 L water for 30 minutes, centrifuging away cells and filter sterilizing the supernatant. The 25% designation is the starting biomass loading, not a claim that the final liquid contains 250 g/L commercial yeast extract.

Hemicalcium D-(+)-pantothenate denotes one-half calcium equivalent per D-pantothenate unit, the same 2:1 D-pantothenate calcium salt represented by CHEBI31345. Official supplier and MediaDive ingredient1123 agree on CAS137-08-6. This supports the raw D-specific alias, but cannot support DL aliases presently on the owner. Four capsaicin names also belong to CHEBI3374 and must be excluded from pantothenate identity matching.

Molar concentration is part of the supplied solution identity. The doubled hyphen is punctuation, but DL is a stereochemical boundary. Sixteen available JCM primary recipes explicitly name DL-Calcium pantothenate. CHEBI180950 is current, nonobsolete Calcium DL-pantothenate, distinct from D-specific CHEBI31345. Its structure lacks stereochemical specification and its CAS cross-reference differs from a supplier DL SDS; no CAS or formula enrichment is inferred from that conflict.

The six JCM originals spell D-Glucose; the doubled source hyphen is punctuation and does not remove D stereochemistry. Current CHEBI17634 explicitly defines D-glucose and includes D(+)-glucose synonyms. Existing D-glucose is the matching D-specific owner.

JCM558 names D-Calcium pantothenate in its seven-vitamin mixture. This agrees with D-specific CHEBI31345 and the salt stoichiometry corroborated by supplier hemicalcium nomenclature. The doubled hyphen is a harmless raw spelling, unlike a DL qualifier.
